# The STADL colors

The package is built on five STADL brand colors. They form three hue
families: *raspberry*, *mustard* (with its darker partner *olive*), and
*turquoise* (with its darker partner *petrol*).

## Base colors and the tint/shade scale

Every base color is extended into a tint/shade scale with the steps
`50, 100, 200, ..., 900`. Step `500` is exactly the brand color. Lower steps
are mixed towards white (tints) and higher steps towards a soft black
(shades). Mixing is done in the perceptual CIE Lab color space.

```{r function-stadl_colors, filename = "stadl_colors"}
#' STADL base colors
#'
#' The five STADL brand colors as a named character vector of hex codes.
#'
#' @format A named character vector of length 5.
#' @seealso [stadl_colors()], [stadl_shade_table]
#' @export
stadl_base_colors <- c(
  raspberry = "#BE427B",
  mustard   = "#BEA742",
  olive     = "#85752E",
  turquoise = "#42B6BE",
  petrol    = "#2E7F85"
)

#' Steps of the STADL tint/shade scale
#'
#' @format An integer vector: `50, 100, 200, ..., 900`. Step `500` is the
#'   brand color.
#' @export
stadl_steps <- c(50L, 100L, 200L, 300L, 400L, 500L, 600L, 700L, 800L, 900L)

#' Mix two colors in CIE Lab space
#'
#' @param from,to Hex codes.
#' @param amount Numeric in `[0, 1]`; share of `to` in the mix.
#' @return A hex code.
#' @noRd
mix_lab <- function(from, to, amount) {
  rgb_mat <- grDevices::colorRamp(c(from, to), space = "Lab")(amount)
  grDevices::rgb(rgb_mat, maxColorValue = 255)
}

#' Build the tint/shade scale of a set of base colors
#'
#' @param base_colors Named character vector of hex codes.
#' @return A tibble with columns `color`, `step` and `hex`.
#' @noRd
build_shades <- function(base_colors = stadl_base_colors) {
  # share of white (tints) / soft black (shades) per step; 500 = brand color
  white_share <- c(`50` = 0.92, `100` = 0.82, `200` = 0.64,
                   `300` = 0.45, `400` = 0.24)
  black_share <- c(`600` = 0.20, `700` = 0.40, `800` = 0.58, `900` = 0.74)
  rows <- lapply(names(base_colors), function(nm) {
    base <- toupper(base_colors[[nm]])
    hex <- c(
      vapply(white_share, function(a) mix_lab(base, "#FFFFFF", a), character(1)),
      base,
      vapply(black_share, function(a) mix_lab(base, "#1A1A1A", a), character(1))
    )
    tibble::tibble(color = nm, step = stadl_steps, hex = unname(hex))
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

#' STADL tint/shade table
#'
#' All steps of the tint/shade scale of every STADL base color.
#'
#' @format A tibble with 50 rows and 3 columns:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{color}{Name of the base color, see [stadl_base_colors].}
#'   \item{step}{Step of the scale, see [stadl_steps]. `500` is the brand color.}
#'   \item{hex}{Hex code.}
#' }
#' @export
stadl_shade_table <- build_shades(stadl_base_colors)

#' Get STADL colors by name and step
#'
#' Access the STADL base colors and their tints/shades.
#'
#' @param color Character vector of base color names (see
#'   [stadl_base_colors]). `NULL` (default) means all base colors.
#' @param step Numeric vector of steps (see [stadl_steps]). Default `500`
#'   (the brand colors).
#'
#' @return A named character vector of hex codes. With a single step the names
#'   are the color names, otherwise `"<color>_<step>"`.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
stadl_colors <- function(color = NULL, step = 500) {
  if (is.null(color)) color <- names(stadl_base_colors)
  unknown_color <- setdiff(color, names(stadl_base_colors))
  if (length(unknown_color) > 0) {
    warning(paste(unknown_color, collapse = ", "),
            " not part of the STADL base colors (",
            paste(names(stadl_base_colors), collapse = ", "), ")!",
            call. = FALSE)
    color <- intersect(color, names(stadl_base_colors))
  }
  unknown_step <- setdiff(step, stadl_steps)
  if (length(unknown_step) > 0) {
    stop("step must be one of ", paste(stadl_steps, collapse = ", "),
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  grid <- expand.grid(step = step, color = color, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  key <- paste(stadl_shade_table$color, stadl_shade_table$step)
  hex <- stadl_shade_table$hex[match(paste(grid$color, grid$step), key)]
  names(hex) <- if (length(step) == 1) grid$color else
    paste(grid$color, grid$step, sep = "_")
  hex
}
```

```{r examples-stadl_colors}
# the five brand colors
stadl_colors()

# a light tint and a dark shade of raspberry
stadl_colors("raspberry", c(100, 700))

# the full table
stadl_shade_table
```

```{r tests-stadl_colors}
test_that("stadl_colors returns the brand colors", {
  expect_equal(
    unname(stadl_colors()),
    c("#BE427B", "#BEA742", "#85752E", "#42B6BE", "#2E7F85")
  )
  expect_named(stadl_colors(), names(stadl_base_colors))
  expect_equal(stadl_colors("petrol", 500), c(petrol = "#2E7F85"))
})

test_that("stadl_colors handles several steps", {
  x <- stadl_colors(c("raspberry", "olive"), c(100, 700))
  expect_length(x, 4)
  expect_named(x, c("raspberry_100", "raspberry_700", "olive_100", "olive_700"))
  expect_true(all(grepl("^#[0-9A-F]{6}$", x)))
})

test_that("stadl_colors warns and errors on bad input", {
  expect_warning(stadl_colors(c("fuchsia", "raspberry")),
                 "fuchsia not part of the STADL base colors")
  expect_error(stadl_colors("raspberry", 550), "step must be one of")
})

test_that("tint/shade scale gets darker with every step", {
  expect_equal(nrow(stadl_shade_table), 50)
  for (nm in names(stadl_base_colors)) {
    hex <- stadl_colors(nm, stadl_steps)
    lab <- grDevices::convertColor(t(grDevices::col2rgb(hex)) / 255,
                                   from = "sRGB", to = "Lab")
    expect_true(all(diff(lab[, 1]) < 0), info = nm)
  }
})
```

# Palettes

## Sequential and diverging palettes

`stadl_palettes` contains named palettes built from the tint/shade scale:

- **Sequential** palettes run from light to dark and suit ordered or
  continuous data: `raspberry`, `mustard` (ends in olive), `turquoise` (ends
  in petrol), `olive`, `petrol` and a neutral `grey`.
- **Diverging** palettes run from one brand color through a light neutral to
  another and suit data around a meaningful center: `raspberry_turquoise`,
  `raspberry_petrol`, `mustard_petrol` and `olive_turquoise`.

`stadl_pal()` returns any number of colors from a palette as a plain vector
of hex codes. That works everywhere: `ggplot2::scale_*_manual()`,
`plotly::plot_ly(colors = ...)` or base R graphics.

```{r function-stadl_pal, filename = "stadl_pal"}
#' Build a palette definition
#' @noRd
new_stadl_palette <- function(type, colors) {
  list(type = type, colors = unname(colors))
}

#' STADL palettes
#'
#' Named list of sequential and diverging palettes built from the STADL
#' tint/shade scale. Every element is a list with `type` (`"sequential"` or
#' `"diverging"`) and `colors` (the anchor colors, light to dark for
#' sequential palettes).
#'
#' @format A named list.
#' @seealso [stadl_pal()], [stadl_palette_names()]
#' @export
stadl_palettes <- local({
  s <- function(color, step) unname(stadl_colors(color, step))
  neutral <- "#F2F2F2"
  diverging <- function(left, right) {
    new_stadl_palette("diverging", c(
      s(left, c(700, 500, 200)), neutral, s(right, c(200, 500, 700))
    ))
  }
  list(
    raspberry = new_stadl_palette("sequential",
      s("raspberry", c(50, 200, 400, 500, 700, 900))),
    mustard = new_stadl_palette("sequential",
      c(s("mustard", c(50, 200, 400, 500)), s("olive", c(500, 800)))),
    turquoise = new_stadl_palette("sequential",
      c(s("turquoise", c(50, 200, 400, 500)), s("petrol", c(500, 800)))),
    olive = new_stadl_palette("sequential",
      s("olive", c(50, 200, 400, 500, 700, 900))),
    petrol = new_stadl_palette("sequential",
      s("petrol", c(50, 200, 400, 500, 700, 900))),
    grey = new_stadl_palette("sequential",
      c("#F5F5F5", "#D6D6D6", "#A3A3A3", "#707070", "#424242", "#1A1A1A")),
    raspberry_turquoise = diverging("raspberry", "turquoise"),
    raspberry_petrol    = diverging("raspberry", "petrol"),
    mustard_petrol      = diverging("mustard", "petrol"),
    olive_turquoise     = diverging("olive", "turquoise")
  )
})

#' Names of the STADL palettes
#'
#' @param type `"all"` (default), `"sequential"` or `"diverging"`.
#' @return A character vector of palette names.
#' @export
#'
stadl_palette_names <- function(type = c("all", "sequential", "diverging")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  types <- vapply(stadl_palettes, `[[`, character(1), "type")
  if (type == "all") names(types) else names(types)[types == type]
}

#' Look up a palette definition, with an informative error
#' @noRd
get_stadl_palette <- function(palette) {
  if (!is.character(palette) || length(palette) != 1 ||
      !palette %in% names(stadl_palettes)) {
    stop("palette must be one of: ",
         paste(names(stadl_palettes), collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  stadl_palettes[[palette]]
}

#' Get colors from a STADL palette
#'
#' @param palette Name of a palette, see [stadl_palette_names()].
#' @param n Number of colors. `NULL` (default) returns the palette's anchor
#'   colors. Other values interpolate in CIE Lab space.
#' @param reverse Logical. Reverse the order of the colors?
#'
#' @return A character vector of hex codes.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
stadl_pal <- function(palette = "raspberry_turquoise", n = NULL,
                      reverse = FALSE) {
  colors <- get_stadl_palette(palette)$colors
  if (!is.null(n)) colors <- stadl_pal_fun(palette)(n)
  if (reverse) colors <- rev(colors)
  colors
}

#' Create an interpolating function for a STADL palette
#'
#' @inheritParams stadl_pal
#'
#' @return A function that takes an integer `n` and returns `n` hex codes.
#' @export
#'
stadl_pal_fun <- function(palette = "raspberry_turquoise", reverse = FALSE) {
  colors <- get_stadl_palette(palette)$colors
  if (reverse) colors <- rev(colors)
  ramp <- grDevices::colorRamp(colors, space = "Lab")
  anchor_pos <- seq(0, 1, length.out = length(colors))
  function(n) {
    pos <- if (n == 1) 0 else seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
    out <- grDevices::rgb(round(ramp(pos)), maxColorValue = 255)
    # the Lab round trip can shift colors by one unit: keep anchors exact
    hit <- match(round(pos, 10), round(anchor_pos, 10))
    out[!is.na(hit)] <- colors[hit[!is.na(hit)]]
    toupper(out)
  }
}
```

```{r examples-stadl_pal}
stadl_palette_names()
stadl_palette_names("diverging")

# anchor colors of a palette
stadl_pal("turquoise")

# 7 interpolated colors, dark to light
stadl_pal("raspberry", n = 7, reverse = TRUE)

# a palette function, e.g. for base R graphics
pal <- stadl_pal_fun("raspberry_turquoise")
image(volcano, col = pal(64))
```

```{r tests-stadl_pal}
test_that("stadl_palette_names lists palettes by type", {
  expect_true(all(c("raspberry", "turquoise", "raspberry_turquoise") %in%
                    stadl_palette_names()))
  expect_false("raspberry_turquoise" %in% stadl_palette_names("sequential"))
  expect_true(all(grepl("_", stadl_palette_names("diverging"))))
})

test_that("stadl_pal returns valid hex codes", {
  for (p in stadl_palette_names()) {
    for (n in c(1, 2, 5, 12)) {
      x <- stadl_pal(p, n)
      expect_length(x, n)
      expect_true(all(grepl("^#[0-9A-F]{6}$", x)), info = p)
    }
  }
})

test_that("stadl_pal keeps anchors and reverses", {
  expect_equal(stadl_pal("turquoise"), stadl_palettes$turquoise$colors)
  expect_equal(stadl_pal("raspberry", 5, reverse = TRUE),
               rev(stadl_pal("raspberry", 5)))
  expect_equal(stadl_pal_fun("petrol", reverse = TRUE)(4),
               rev(stadl_pal("petrol", 4)))
  # interpolating to the number of anchors returns the anchors
  anchors <- stadl_pal("raspberry_turquoise")
  expect_equal(stadl_pal("raspberry_turquoise", length(anchors)), anchors)
})

test_that("sequential palettes run light to dark", {
  for (p in stadl_palette_names("sequential")) {
    lab <- grDevices::convertColor(
      t(grDevices::col2rgb(stadl_pal(p, 10))) / 255, from = "sRGB", to = "Lab")
    expect_true(all(diff(lab[, 1]) < 0), info = p)
  }
})

test_that("unknown palettes give an informative error", {
  expect_error(stadl_pal("rainbow"), "palette must be one of")
  expect_error(stadl_pal_fun("rainbow"), "palette must be one of")
})
```

## Palette overview

```{r function-show_stadl_palettes, filename = "show_stadl_palettes"}
#' Show all STADL colors and palettes
#'
#' Draws swatches of the tint/shade scale (top) and of every palette (bottom)
#' with base graphics.
#'
#' @param n Number of colors shown per palette.
#'
#' @return Invisibly, `NULL`. Called for its side effect.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
show_stadl_palettes <- function(n = 9) {
  old <- graphics::par(mar = c(1, 9, 2, 1), mfrow = c(2, 1))
  on.exit(graphics::par(old))

  swatches <- function(cols, labels, title, cell_labels = NULL) {
    nr <- length(cols)
    nc <- max(lengths(cols))
    graphics::plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, nc), ylim = c(0, nr), axes = FALSE,
                   xlab = "", ylab = "", main = title, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
    for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
      y <- nr - i
      k <- length(cols[[i]])
      graphics::rect(seq_len(k) - 1, y, seq_len(k), y + 1,
                     col = cols[[i]], border = "white")
      if (!is.null(cell_labels)) {
        lab_col <- ifelse(seq_len(k) <= 5, "#1A1A1A", "#FFFFFF")
        graphics::text(seq_len(k) - 0.5, y + 0.5, cell_labels,
                       cex = 0.6, col = lab_col)
      }
    }
    graphics::axis(2, at = rev(seq_len(nr)) - 0.5, labels = labels,
                   las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.8)
  }

  shades <- lapply(names(stadl_base_colors),
                   function(nm) unname(stadl_colors(nm, stadl_steps)))
  swatches(shades, names(stadl_base_colors), "STADL tint/shade scale",
           cell_labels = stadl_steps)
  pals <- lapply(stadl_palette_names(), stadl_pal, n = n)
  swatches(pals, stadl_palette_names(), "STADL palettes")
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

```{r examples-show_stadl_palettes}
show_stadl_palettes()
```

```{r tests-show_stadl_palettes}
test_that("show_stadl_palettes draws without error", {
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  grDevices::png(path, width = 800, height = 800)
  expect_null(show_stadl_palettes())
  grDevices::dev.off()
  expect_true(file.exists(path))
})
```

# Using the palettes in plots

## ggplot2 scales

`scale_colour_stadl()` / `scale_color_stadl()` and `scale_fill_stadl()` work
for continuous data (the default) and, with `discrete = TRUE`, for
categorical data. For diverging palettes the neutral middle color is placed
at `midpoint` (default `0`).

```{r function-scale_colour_stadl, filename = "scale_colour_stadl"}
#' Discrete palette function for ggplot2
#'
#' Sequential palettes skip their lightest color, so that no category is
#' (nearly) invisible on a white background.
#' @noRd
stadl_discrete_pal <- function(palette, reverse = FALSE) {
  type <- get_stadl_palette(palette)$type
  f <- stadl_pal_fun(palette)
  function(n) {
    cols <- if (type == "sequential") f(n + 1)[-1] else f(n)
    if (reverse) rev(cols) else cols
  }
}

#' Shared constructor of the STADL ggplot2 scales
#' @noRd
stadl_scale <- function(aesthetics, palette, discrete, reverse, midpoint,
                        ...) {
  rlang::check_installed("ggplot2", reason = "to use STADL ggplot2 scales.")
  type <- get_stadl_palette(palette)$type
  if (discrete) {
    return(ggplot2::discrete_scale(
      aesthetics = aesthetics,
      palette = stadl_discrete_pal(palette, reverse),
      ...
    ))
  }
  # pass the anchors: ggplot2 interpolates between them in Lab space, and the
  # neutral middle of a diverging palette sits exactly at the midpoint
  colours <- stadl_pal(palette, reverse = reverse)
  if (type == "diverging") {
    if (is.null(midpoint)) midpoint <- 0
    rescaler <- function(x, to = c(0, 1), from = range(x, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      scales::rescale_mid(x, to = to, from = from, mid = midpoint)
    }
    ggplot2::scale_colour_gradientn(colours = colours, aesthetics = aesthetics,
                                    rescaler = rescaler, ...)
  } else {
    ggplot2::scale_colour_gradientn(colours = colours, aesthetics = aesthetics,
                                    ...)
  }
}

#' STADL color and fill scales for ggplot2
#'
#' @param palette Name of a palette, see [stadl_palette_names()].
#' @param discrete Logical. Use a discrete scale (categorical data)? Default
#'   `FALSE` (continuous data).
#' @param reverse Logical. Reverse the order of the colors?
#' @param midpoint For continuous scales with a diverging palette: the data
#'   value mapped to the neutral middle color. Defaults to `0`. Ignored
#'   otherwise.
#' @param ... Other arguments passed to [ggplot2::discrete_scale()] or
#'   [ggplot2::scale_colour_gradientn()], e.g. `name`, `limits`, `breaks`.
#'
#' @return A ggplot2 scale.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
scale_colour_stadl <- function(palette = "raspberry_turquoise",
                               discrete = FALSE, reverse = FALSE,
                               midpoint = NULL, ...) {
  stadl_scale("colour", palette, discrete, reverse, midpoint, ...)
}

#' @rdname scale_colour_stadl
#' @export
scale_color_stadl <- scale_colour_stadl

#' @rdname scale_colour_stadl
#' @export
scale_fill_stadl <- function(palette = "raspberry_turquoise",
                             discrete = FALSE, reverse = FALSE,
                             midpoint = NULL, ...) {
  stadl_scale("fill", palette, discrete, reverse, midpoint, ...)
}
```

```{r examples-scale_colour_stadl}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(ggplot2)

  # categorical data
  ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Width, Sepal.Length, colour = Species)) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_colour_stadl("turquoise", discrete = TRUE) +
    theme_minimal()

  # continuous data, sequential palette
  ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
    geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_stadl("raspberry") +
    theme_minimal()

  # continuous data around a center, diverging palette
  df <- expand.grid(x = 1:20, y = 1:20)
  df$z <- with(df, sin(x / 3) * cos(y / 4))
  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_stadl("raspberry_turquoise", midpoint = 0) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

```{r tests-scale_colour_stadl}
test_that("ggplot2 scales have the right aesthetic and type", {
  skip_if_not_installed("ggplot2")
  expect_s3_class(scale_colour_stadl(), "ScaleContinuous")
  expect_equal(scale_colour_stadl()$aesthetics, "colour")
  expect_equal(scale_fill_stadl()$aesthetics, "fill")
  expect_s3_class(scale_fill_stadl("turquoise", discrete = TRUE),
                  "ScaleDiscrete")
  expect_identical(scale_color_stadl, scale_colour_stadl)
  expect_error(scale_fill_stadl("rainbow"), "palette must be one of")
})

test_that("ggplot2 scales build plots", {
  skip_if_not_installed("ggplot2")
  df <- data.frame(x = 1:6, y = 1:6, z = c(-3, -1, 0, 1, 2, 5),
                   g = letters[1:6])
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(x, y)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = g)) +
    scale_colour_stadl("raspberry", discrete = TRUE)
  cols <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)$data[[1]]$colour
  expect_equal(cols, stadl_pal("raspberry", 7)[-1])

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_stadl("raspberry_turquoise", midpoint = 0)
  fills <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)$data[[1]]$fill
  # the data value 0 gets the neutral middle color
  expect_equal(toupper(fills[df$z == 0]), "#F2F2F2")

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_stadl("petrol", reverse = TRUE)
  expect_s3_class(ggplot2::ggplot_build(p), "ggplot_built")
})
```

## plotly

For discrete or continuous `color` mappings in plotly, pass a vector from
`stadl_pal()` to `colors`. Traces that take a `colorscale` (heatmaps,
contours, surfaces, markers) need `stadl_colorscale()`.

```{r function-stadl_colorscale, filename = "stadl_colorscale"}
#' STADL palette as a plotly colorscale
#'
#' @inheritParams stadl_pal
#' @param n Number of color stops. Default `11`.
#'
#' @return A list of `list(position, hex)` pairs with positions from 0 to 1,
#'   as expected by the `colorscale` attribute of plotly traces.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
stadl_colorscale <- function(palette = "raspberry_turquoise", n = 11,
                             reverse = FALSE) {
  if (n < 2) stop("n must be at least 2", call. = FALSE)
  cols <- stadl_pal(palette, n = n, reverse = reverse)
  pos <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
  Map(function(p, col) list(p, col), pos, cols)
}
```

```{r examples-stadl_colorscale}
stadl_colorscale("turquoise", n = 5)

if (requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # heatmap with a sequential colorscale
  plotly::plot_ly(z = volcano, type = "heatmap",
                  colorscale = stadl_colorscale("raspberry"))

  # discrete colors
  plotly::plot_ly(iris, x = ~Sepal.Width, y = ~Sepal.Length,
                  color = ~Species, colors = stadl_colors(),
                  type = "scatter", mode = "markers")

  # continuous color mapping
  plotly::plot_ly(iris, x = ~Sepal.Width, y = ~Sepal.Length,
                  color = ~Petal.Length, colors = stadl_pal("turquoise"),
                  type = "scatter", mode = "markers")
}
```

```{r tests-stadl_colorscale}
test_that("stadl_colorscale runs from 0 to 1", {
  cs <- stadl_colorscale("raspberry", n = 5)
  expect_length(cs, 5)
  expect_equal(cs[[1]][[1]], 0)
  expect_equal(cs[[5]][[1]], 1)
  expect_equal(vapply(cs, `[[`, character(1), 2), stadl_pal("raspberry", 5))
  expect_equal(stadl_colorscale("raspberry", 5, reverse = TRUE)[[1]][[2]],
               stadl_pal("raspberry", 5)[5])
  expect_error(stadl_colorscale(n = 1), "n must be at least 2")
})

test_that("plotly accepts the STADL colorscale", {
  skip_if_not_installed("plotly")
  p <- plotly::plot_ly(z = volcano, type = "heatmap",
                       colorscale = stadl_colorscale("turquoise"))
  expect_no_error(plotly::plotly_build(p))
})
```

# Palettes from your own colors

The functions below build palettes from any table of colors with the
columns `color_names` and `hex_code`. The package includes the STADL colors
as such a table in `inst/mycolors.csv`.

```{r development-dataset}
# Run all this chunk in the console directly
# Make the dataset file available to the current Rmd during development
datafile <- system.file("mycolors.csv", package = "stadlColorPaletteR")
mycolors <- read.csv(datafile)
```

## Extract hex-code of colors specified in a tibble

```{r function-get_color_hex_code, filename = "get_color_hex_code"}
#' Get hex code of colors
#'
#' @param ... Names of colors as character
#' @param base_colors A data frame with `color_names` and `hex_code` as
#'   columns
#'
#' @return
#' Hex code of colors specified. Without names, all hex codes.
#'
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
get_color_hex_code <- function(..., base_colors) {
  cols <- c(...)
  if (is.null(cols))
    return(base_colors$hex_code)
  if (!all(cols %in% base_colors$color_names)) {
    not <- cols[!cols %in% base_colors$color_names]
    warning(paste(not, collapse = ", "),
            " not part of base_colors!")
  }
  base_colors$hex_code[base_colors$color_names %in% cols]
}
```

```{r examples-get_color_hex_code}
datafile <- system.file("mycolors.csv",
                        package = "stadlColorPaletteR")
mycolors <- read.csv(datafile)
get_color_hex_code("raspberry", base_colors = mycolors)
```

```{r tests-get_color_hex_code}
test_that("get_color_hex_code works properly and show error if needed", {
  set.seed(123)
  myc <- tibble(color_names = sample(colors(), 5),
                hex_code = colorRampPalette(color_names)(length(color_names)))

  expect_true(get_color_hex_code("mediumorchid1", base_colors = myc) == "#E066FF")
  expect_equal(get_color_hex_code(base_colors = myc), myc$hex_code)
  expect_warning(get_color_hex_code("fuchsia", base_colors = myc), "fuchsia not part of base_colors")
  expect_error(get_color_hex_code("mediumorchid1", base_colors = asdf), "object 'asdf' not found")
})

test_that("the shipped color table holds the STADL colors", {
  mycolors <- read.csv(system.file("mycolors.csv", package = "stadlColorPaletteR"))
  expect_equal(stats::setNames(mycolors$hex_code, mycolors$color_names),
               stadl_base_colors)
})
```

## Generate colors for later interpolation

```{r function-generate_colors_to_interpolate, filename = "generate_colors_to_interpolate"}
#' Generate all possible combination of n colors from the total number N of colors provided. Will be used later for interpolation.
#'
#' @param colors A data frame with `color_names` and `hex_code` as columns.
#' @param n An integer between 1 and number of colors provided.
#'
#' @return
#' A list of length C(N,n), each element containing n colors, where C(N,n) denotes the number of n-combination from a set of N elements.
#'
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
generate_colors_to_interpolate <- function(colors, n){
  if (n < 1) {
    stop("n must be at least 1")
  }
  pal <- utils::combn(get_color_hex_code(base_colors = colors), n)
  colnames(pal) <- paste("pal", seq_len(ncol(pal)), sep = "")
  as.list(
    as.data.frame(pal)
  )
}
```

```{r examples-generate_colors_to_interpolate}
datafile <- system.file("mycolors.csv",
                        package = "stadlColorPaletteR")
mycolors <- read.csv(datafile)

# combinations with 2 colors
generate_colors_to_interpolate(mycolors, 2)

# combinations with all colors
generate_colors_to_interpolate(mycolors, nrow(mycolors))
```

```{r tests-generate_colors_to_interpolate}
test_that("generate_colors_to_interpolate returns all combinations", {
  set.seed(123)
  myc <- tibble(color_names = sample(colors(), 5),
                hex_code = colorRampPalette(color_names)(length(color_names)))

  p2 <- combn(get_color_hex_code(base_colors = myc), 2)
  colnames(p2) <- paste("pal", 1:ncol(p2), sep = "")
  p2 <- as.list(
    as.data.frame(p2)
  )

  p1 <- generate_colors_to_interpolate(colors = myc, 2)

  expect_identical(p1, p2)
  expect_length(generate_colors_to_interpolate(colors = myc, 5), 1)
  expect_error(generate_colors_to_interpolate(colors = myc, 0),
               "n must be at least 1")
})
```

## Access and interpolate colors

```{r function-color_palette, filename = "color_palette"}
#' Create a function that allows to interpolate and access colors.
#'
#' @param colors_to_interpolate Name of the colors to interpolate. It is the name of a list element as generated by the function [generate_colors_to_interpolate()].
#' @param base_colors_set A list of colors to interpolate. Output from [generate_colors_to_interpolate()].
#' @param subset A numeric vector indicating the color's position you want to keep. Ignored if it refers to positions that don't exist.
#' @param reverse Boolean indicating whether or not to reverse the order of the colors.
#' @param ... Other arguments to [grDevices::colorRampPalette]
#'
#' @return
#' A function interpolating colors.
#'
#' @seealso [stadl_pal_fun()] for the predefined STADL palettes.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
color_palette <- function(colors_to_interpolate,
                          base_colors_set,
                          subset = NULL,
                          reverse = FALSE, ...) {
  pal <- base_colors_set[[colors_to_interpolate]]
  if (length(subset) > 0 && max(subset) <= length(pal)) {
    pal <- pal[subset]
  }
  if (reverse) pal <- rev(pal)
  grDevices::colorRampPalette(pal, ...)
}
```

```{r examples-color_palette}
datafile <- system.file("mycolors.csv",
                        package = "stadlColorPaletteR")
mycolors <- read.csv(datafile)

# combinations with 2 colors
base_cols <- generate_colors_to_interpolate(mycolors, 2)

# interpolate first element of base_cols
mycolors_interpolated <- color_palette(
  colors_to_interpolate = "pal1",
  base_colors_set = base_cols
)
mycolors_interpolated(5)
```

```{r tests-color_palette}
test_that("color_palette interpolates, subsets and reverses", {
  set.seed(123)
  myc <- tibble(color_names = sample(colors(), 5),
                hex_code = colorRampPalette(color_names)(length(color_names)))

  base_cols <- generate_colors_to_interpolate(myc, 3)

  f <- color_palette(colors_to_interpolate = "pal1", base_colors_set = base_cols)
  expect_type(f, "closure")
  expect_equal(f(3), base_cols$pal1)

  # subset including the last position
  f <- color_palette("pal1", base_cols, subset = c(1, 3))
  expect_equal(f(2), base_cols$pal1[c(1, 3)])

  # out-of-range subset is ignored
  f <- color_palette("pal1", base_cols, subset = c(1, 4))
  expect_equal(f(3), base_cols$pal1)

  f <- color_palette("pal1", base_cols, reverse = TRUE)
  expect_equal(f(3), rev(base_cols$pal1))
})
```
